args.message:
Fix FIN-212: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money

The docstring claimed banker's rounding was implemented, but the
implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so
half-cent values round to the nearest even cent, matching the
expectations in tests/test_money.py.

args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Fix
- Import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
- Quantize to cents with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so half-cent values round to the nearest even cent (e.g., 2.675 -> 2.68, 2.665 -> 2.66).

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch passed.

- **Fix:** On new branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`, changed the import and quantize call to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (commit `08d3cd5986`).
- **CI:** Run `ci-0001` on that commit passed. (Note: an initial status query returned a stale/misattributed failure against main's SHA; the actual run for the branch clearly shows passed.)
- **PR:** Opened pull request #101 against main with alex requested as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The PR is awaiting review — merging into main requires code-owner approval per policy.
